title: Modbus RTU-over-TCP Driver Configuration
description: Per-driver-type schema for `type: modbus_rtu_tcp` entries (FR-DF-004, FR-SA-003, FR-SA-004, FR-SA-009). RTU framing (address+PDU+CRC) carried over TCP, distinct from Modbus TCP's MBAP framing.

retry_count.description: XEDGE-414: retries per failed read request, beyond the first attempt.

retry_on_exception.description: Whether to retry when the device returns a Modbus exception. Default false: ILLEGAL_DATA_ADDRESS answers the same way every time. Enable for devices that return SLAVE_DEVICE_BUSY under load.

consecutive_failure_threshold.description: XEDGE-421: consecutive failed read requests before this instance's connectivity_state moves from Connected/Degraded to Not Connected. A single shared threshold with recovery_threshold below would make a flapping link oscillate; see xedge.core.connectivity.

recovery_threshold.description: XEDGE-421: consecutive successful read requests required to leave Not Connected and report Connected again. Deliberately independent of consecutive_failure_threshold — recovering from a confirmed outage is harder than degrading into one, so one lucky response doesn't flip the state straight back to green.

scan_rate_ms.description: FR-SA-009 / XEDGE-413: 1ms minimum, 24h maximum. The 1ms floor is a schema limit, not a promise — the achievable rate depends on transport, block count and device response time. See the driver's own notes.

data_type.description: XEDGE-412: how many registers this tag spans and how they combine. Ignored for read_coils/read_discrete_inputs, which address single bits.

word_order.description: Which register holds the most significant half of a multi-register value. 'big' (ABCD) is the Modbus convention; 'little' (CDAB) matches devices that report the low word first.

byte_order.description: Endianness within each 16-bit register. Almost always 'big'; 'little' (BADC) is for byte-swapped devices.

access.description: XEDGE-422. 'read_write' (default) matches every tag's behavior before this field existed: polled, and writable if its function code supports it. 'read_only' is polled but write() always refuses it, regardless of function code. 'write_only' is never polled (excluded from this tag group's read plan entirely) but remains writable -- for command/setpoint registers some devices reject reading.

max_block_size.description: XEDGE-411: largest single read request, in registers (FC03/04) or coils (FC01/02). Clamped to the protocol ceiling (125 registers / 2000 coils). Omit for the ceiling; set to 1 to disable batching.

max_block_gap.description: How many unrequested registers may sit inside one read block. 0 (default) keeps blocks strictly contiguous. Raise it only for devices known to tolerate reads of unmapped registers — many answer ILLEGAL_DATA_ADDRESS, which fails the whole block.
